mainTopic: Wine touched by a גוי without intent (forbidden to drink, allowed for benefit), רב's rule about a one-day-old baby, and when bought slaves stop making wine into יין נסך
overview: The גמרא first asks why שמואל held off on ruling about wine a גוי touched. It rejects the idea that he feared a strict תנא like רבי נתן, and concludes he hoped to find a lenient תנא like רבי שמעון so he could allow even drinking. Next comes a story in בירם: a גוי's palm branch touched wine by accident, and רב allowed it to be sold to גוים. When challenged with his own rule that even a one-day-old גוי baby makes wine into יין נסך, רב explains that such a touch forbids drinking but not benefit. רב שימי בר חייא then challenges that baby rule from a ברייתא saying young slaves who don't understand idol worship do not forbid wine. The גמרא limits that leniency to sons of maidservants raised in a Jewish home. It then works through the ברייתא's word וכן and reads it to mean that slaves, once circumcised and immersed, no longer forbid wine. This reading goes against רב נחמן in the name of שמואל, who said bought slaves forbid wine until עבודה זרה is gone from their mouths, which רבי יהושע בן לוי sets at twelve months. רבה begins challenging רב נחמן from the same ברייתא, and that challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A first suggested reason for שמואל's delay
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that שמואל held off on ruling because he might find a תנא like רבי נתן, which would force him to forbid even benefit from the wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe שמואל waited because he thought: if I find a תנא who forbids this wine the way רבי נתן does, I will forbid even getting benefit from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is giving a first possible reason why שמואל delayed his ruling: he was worried about a stricter opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion is that שמואל leaned toward allowing benefit, but held back in case a stricter תנא (like רבי נתן) existed. If so, the wine would be forbidden even for selling. The next step brings the source for רבי נתן's strict view.

keyTerms.meaning: I find
a sage from the time of the משנה
forbids
benefit (for example, selling the wine), as opposed to drinking it

phrases.english: Because if I find a tanna
phrases.notes: This is שמואל's thinking, explaining why he delayed his ruling on the case discussed just before this.

phrases.english: who prohibits in accordance with Rabbi Natan,
I will prohibit it even for benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי מַשְׁכַּחְנָא תַּנָּא דְּאָסַר כְּרַבִּי נָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section as a proposed explanation of שמואל's delay, which was discussed before this point.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל feared a stricter תנא like רבי נתן who would forbid even benefit.

steps.title: The ברייתא showing רבי נתן's strict view
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי נתן forbids wine that a גוי measured with his hand, while the תנא קמא allows it to be sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: if a גוי measured the wine, whether with his hand or his foot, it may be sold. רבי נתן says: with his hand it is forbidden; with his foot it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source showing that רבי נתן is stricter than the other opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion lets the wine be sold in both cases. רבי נתן forbids it when the measuring was by hand, which means he forbids even selling it. He still allows the foot case.

keyTerms.meaning: he measured it (checked the wine's depth)
it may be sold
with the foot

phrases.english: As it is taught: If he measured it,
phrases.notes: He means a גוי who measured a Jew's wine.

phrases.english: whether with the hand or with the foot, it may be sold.
Rabbi Natan says:
With the hand, it is prohibited; with the foot, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the רבי נתן opinion mentioned in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a תנא, רבי נתן, who forbids benefit from wine a גוי touched.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about a גוי measuring wine by hand or by foot.

steps.title: רבי נתן only forbids the hand case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the first reason: רבי נתן forbids only hand-measuring, and he permits the foot case, so his view would not forbid our case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine, רבי נתן said the hand case is forbidden. Did he say the foot case is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggested reason from step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן himself permits wine measured with the foot. So his strictness is limited to direct hand contact, and he would not forbid benefit in a case like שמואל's. That means fear of רבי נתן cannot explain why שמואל waited.

keyTerms.meaning: say, grant that
did he say? (meaning: he did not)

phrases.english: Say that Rabbi Natan said this regarding the hand;
did he say it regarding the foot?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דְּאָמַר רַבִּי נָתָן בַּיָּד, בָּרֶגֶל מִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation of step 1 using the details of the ברייתא in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שמואל delayed out of fear of רבי נתן's strict view.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי נתן is strict only about the hand and openly permits the foot, so he gives no basis to forbid benefit in שמואל's case.

steps.title: The real reason: hoping to find a lenient תנא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא flips the reason: שמואל delayed because, if he found a תנא like רבי שמעון, he could permit the wine even for drinking.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, שמואל thought: if I find a תנא who permits this the way רבי שמעון does, I will permit it even for drinking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא replaces the rejected reason with the opposite one: שמואל was hoping to be more lenient, not more strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Benefit was already allowed. The question was whether drinking could also be allowed. רבי שמעון holds that a גוי's touch without intent does not forbid the wine, so finding support for his view would let שמואל allow drinking too.

keyTerms.meaning: rather (rejects the earlier idea and gives a new one)
permits
drinking

steps.whatToRemember: In שמואל's case, benefit was permitted. His delay was only about whether drinking could also be permitted, following רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: Rather, because if I find a tanna
who permits in accordance with Rabbi Shimon,
I will permit it even for drinking.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּאִי מַשְׁכַּחְנָא תַּנָּא דְּשָׁרֵי כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 by offering a new reason for שמואל's delay.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the explanation: the delay pointed toward leniency, not strictness.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל delayed because he feared a stricter opinion that forbids benefit.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל delayed because he hoped for a lenient opinion that would allow even drinking.

steps.title: The story in בירם: a palm branch touches wine
steps.stepSummary: A גוי's palm branch touched wine by accident, and רב allowed the wine to be sold to גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a case in בירם. A גוי climbed a palm tree and brought down a palm branch. As he came down, the tip of the branch touched some wine without his meaning to. רב allowed the owners to sell the wine to גוים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story with a ruling by רב about wine that a גוי touched unintentionally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The touch was both indirect (through a branch) and accidental. רב allowed selling the wine, meaning benefit is permitted. He did not allow drinking it, which sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: an incident, a real case
a palm tree
a palm branch
without intent, by accident
to sell it

phrases.english: There was a certain incident that happened in Biram,
where a certain gentile was
climbing a palm tree
and he brought down a palm branch.
While he was descending,
he touched, with the tip of the palm branch,
the wine, unintentionally.
Rav permitted selling it to gentiles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related case about unintentional touching, this time with a ruling by רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine touched unintentionally by a גוי through a palm branch may be sold to גוים.

steps.title: רב כהנא and רב אסי challenge רב from his own rule
steps.stepSummary: רב's students point out that רב himself said even a one-day-old גוי baby, who has no intent at all, makes wine into יין נסך.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא and רב אסי said to רב: But you yourself said that a one-day-old baby makes wine into יין נסך!
steps.whatsHappening: רב's students challenge his lenient ruling by quoting another ruling of his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A newborn has no intent at all, yet רב said his touch makes wine forbidden. So lack of intent should not help, and the wine in בירם should be forbidden too. The challenge assumes that יין נסך is forbidden in every way, including benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: but isn't it you, Master, who said
a one-day-old baby
wine used for (or treated as) an idolatrous offering, which is forbidden

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא וְרַב אַסִּי לְרַב,
phrases.english: Rav Kahana and Rav Asi said to Rav:
But isn't it you, Master, who said:
A one-day-old baby
phrases.notes: He means a גוי baby who touches the wine.

phrases.english: renders it libation wine!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's permission to sell wine touched unintentionally.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a baby with no intent forbids wine, then an accidental touch should forbid it too, and the wine should not be sold.

steps.title: רב: my rule forbids drinking, not benefit
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that his rule about the baby only forbids drinking; it never forbade benefit, so selling is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Fine, I said it is forbidden for drinking. Did I say it is forbidden for benefit?
steps.whatsHappening: רב resolves the contradiction by limiting what his baby rule forbids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A touch without intent forbids drinking the wine but does not forbid benefit from it. That fits both rulings: the baby's touch makes the wine forbidden to drink, and the wine in בירם cannot be drunk but may be sold.

keyTerms.meaning: say that I said (granting a point, but only so far)
did I say? (meaning: I did not)

steps.whatToRemember: When a גוי touches wine without intent, the wine is forbidden to drink but permitted for benefit, such as selling it to גוים.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב called the wine fully permitted. It is still forbidden to drink. He only allowed selling it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This split between drinking and benefit is the key idea of the whole section, and it matches the conclusion about שמואל's case above.

phrases.english: He said to them:
Say that I said it regarding drinking;
did I say it regarding benefit?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימוֹר דַּאֲמַרִי אֲנָא בִּשְׁתִיָּיה, בַּהֲנָאָה מִי אֲמַרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 and supports the ruling of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of רב's earlier rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's baby rule forbids the wine completely, even for benefit.
steps.terutzMaskana: A touch without intent forbids only drinking; benefit is permitted.

steps.title: Back to רב's rule about the one-day-old baby
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רב's statement that a one-day-old gentile baby makes wine into יין נסך, so it can examine that statement directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the statement itself: רב said that a gentile baby only one day old makes wine into יין נסך.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is going back to quote רב's rule about the baby, which was mentioned in passing in step 6. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6 this rule was only used as a tool to question רב about the palm branch. Now the גמרא puts the rule itself on the table, because it wants to test whether it is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: "The thing itself." The גמרא is going back to discuss a statement it quoted earlier.
A baby only one day old, who has no understanding or intent at all.

phrases.english: Now to the matter itself: Rav said:
phrases.notes: This is the rule רב's students quoted back to him in step 6. Now the גמרא looks at it on its own.

phrases.english: A baby one day old
makes wine into libation wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the baby rule, which steps 6-7 only used as a side point, and makes it the main topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a one-day-old gentile baby, who has no intent at all, makes wine he touches into יין נסך (forbidden to drink).

steps.title: A ברייתא about circumcised slaves who have not immersed
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר חייא quotes a ברייתא about slaves who were circumcised but have not immersed. It says adults make wine יין נסך, but minors, meaning those who do not understand idol worship, do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר חייא challenged רב from a ברייתא: Slaves bought from גוים, or sons of maidservants, who were circumcised but did not immerse are still treated like גוים. Their spit and what they tread on in the market is impure, and some say pure. As for their wine, the adults make it יין נסך and the minors do not. Who counts as an adult? One who understands idol worship and its objects. Who counts as a minor? One who does not understand them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר חייא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב. This step quotes the source, and the next step points out exactly where it clashes with רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The slaves in the ברייתא are not yet full converts, so they are treated like גוים. Even so, the ברייתא says only the ones who understand idol worship make wine forbidden. That depends on understanding, while רב said even a baby with no understanding forbids wine.

keyTerms.meaning: They were circumcised but did not immerse in a מקוה, so their conversion is not finished.
Sons of non-Jewish maidservants, who grew up in a Jewish home.
Things they press on by treading or sitting, which can become impure from them.
They understand what idol worship is all about.

steps.confusionAlert: In this ברייתא, "adult" and "minor" are not about age in years. They depend on whether the person understands idol worship and its objects.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב שִׁימִי בַּר חִיָּיא לְרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ḥiyya raised an objection to Rav:
One who buys slaves from the gentiles,
who were circumcised but did not immerse,
and likewise the sons of the maidservants,
who were circumcised but did not immerse —
their spit and what they tread on in the marketplace is impure,
and some say: it is pure.
As for their wine:
adults make it libation wine,
minors do not make it libation wine.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן גְּדוֹלִים וְאֵלּוּ הֵן קְטַנִּים?
phrases.english: And who are the adults, and who are the minors?
Adults are those who know the nature
of idol worship and its accessories,
minors are those who do not know the nature
of idol worship and its accessories.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב שִׁימִי בַּר חִיָּיא לְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to attack the rule stated in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that a one-day-old gentile baby makes wine into יין נסך.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא makes forbidding wine depend on understanding idol worship. A baby understands nothing, so by the ברייתא he should not forbid wine.

steps.title: Pinpointing the clash: minors do not forbid wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the problem: the ברייתא says adults forbid wine but minors do not, which goes against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the ברייתא teaches that adults do forbid wine and minors do not, which goes against רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to the exact line of the ברייתא that contradicts רב: minors do not make wine יין נסך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the ברייתא, about impurity, doesn't matter here, which is why the גמרא says "in any case." What matters is that a young slave who knows nothing does not forbid wine, while רב said even a one-day-old does.

keyTerms.meaning: "In any case it teaches." It focuses on the one part of a source that matters for the argument.
Yes.
No.

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches:
adults, yes,
minors, no!
phrases.notes: This is the problem: רב said even a one-day-old baby makes the wine forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the ברייתא quoted in step 9 and draws out the exact point that contradicts רב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If young slaves with no understanding do not forbid wine, then a one-day-old gentile baby should not forbid it either.

steps.title: The ברייתא is talking about sons of maidservants
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the adult/minor split applies only to sons of maidservants, who grow up in a Jewish home, not to ordinary gentile children.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא's rule about adults and minors was explained as referring only to the sons of the maidservants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by limiting the ברייתא's rule about minors to children of maidservants raised in a Jewish home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Children raised in a Jewish home are not used to idol worship, so the חכמים did not forbid wine touched by the young ones. A slave bought from גוים, or an ordinary gentile baby, is different. So רב's rule still applies to them.

keyTerms.meaning: "He explained it." The source is read as applying to a narrower case.

steps.whatToRemember: רב's rule stands: an ordinary gentile baby, even one day old, makes wine into יין נסך. The ברייתא's exception for minors covers only sons of maidservants raised in a Jewish home.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the leniency for young children is tied to being raised among Jews, not to the child's age alone.

phrases.english: He explained it as referring to the sons of the maidservants.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 9-10 by narrowing the case the ברייתא is talking about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a specific case (בני שפחות only).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that any young gentile child with no understanding does not forbid wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only young sons of maidservants raised in a Jewish home do not forbid wine. Other gentile babies do, just as רב said.

steps.title: But the ברייתא says 'And so too'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 11: the ברייתא uses וכן, which links slaves and sons of maidservants, so the adult/minor split should apply to both.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא says 'and so too'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 11. The ברייתא joins bought slaves and sons of maidservants with the word וכן ('and so too'), so how can we split them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said the adult/minor split only applies to sons of maidservants, who grow up in a Jewish home. But וכן seems to say that slaves and sons of maidservants have the same rule. If so, the split applies to ordinary slaves too, and רב's ruling about a one-day-old baby is in trouble again.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And so too': a word that joins two cases to the same rule
It says / it is saying

phrases.english: But it says 'and so too'!
phrases.notes: The ברייתא lists the slaves and then says 'and so too' the sons of maidservants, putting them together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 11's claim that the adult/minor split applies only to sons of maidservants.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word וכן in the ברייתא equates slaves with sons of maidservants, so they should not be split.

steps.title: The link is only about spit and what they step on
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that וכן equates the two groups only regarding the טומאה of their spit and of objects they step on.
steps.simpleTranslation: It links them regarding their spit and what they step on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that וכן does not link the two groups about wine at all. It only says that both have the same טומאה rule for their spit and for what they step on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By moving וכן to a different topic, the גמרא keeps step 11 safe. The two groups can share a טומאה rule and still be different in the adult/minor rule for wine. So רב's ruling still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Their spit
Objects they step on, sit on, or lean on, which can become טמא through their pressure

phrases.english: Regarding their spit and what they tread upon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the word וכן to a different law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: וכן equates slaves and sons of maidservants regarding wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: וכן equates them only regarding the טומאה of their spit and what they step on.

steps.title: That answer only works for the opinion that holds they are טמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the answer only works for the opinion that their spit and what they step on are טמא. For the opinion that they are טהור, וכן has nothing to teach about טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who says they are טמא. But for the one who says they are טהור, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 13. There is a disagreement about whether these slaves' spit and what they step on are טמא or טהור, and step 13 only works for one side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If they are טמא, it makes sense for the ברייתא to tell us the sons of maidservants share that rule. But if they are טהור, it is obvious that sons of maidservants are טהור too, and there is nothing to teach. So for that opinion, וכן must be about wine after all, and the problem from step 12 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out fine
According to the one who says
Ritually impure
Ritually pure
What can be said? (a phrase that challenges an answer)

phrases.english: This works out well according to the one who says they are impure,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the spit and the things the slaves step on.

phrases.english: but according to the one who says they are pure,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר טָמֵא, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר טָהוֹר, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 13's claim that וכן refers only to spit and what they step on.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For the opinion that holds they are טהור, there is nothing new to teach about טומאה, so וכן must refer to wine.

steps.title: Slaves are like sons of maidservants: immersion ends the problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that וכן is about wine, but only to teach that slaves are like sons of maidservants: once circumcised and immersed, they no longer make wine into יין נסך.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us that slaves are like sons of maidservants. Just as sons of maidservants who were circumcised but did not immerse make wine into יין נסך, but once circumcised and immersed they do not, so too with slaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees that וכן is about wine. But it says the link is not about the adult/minor split; it is about what happens after immersion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before immersion, these people still make wine into יין נסך. After circumcision and immersion, sons of maidservants clearly do not, and וכן teaches that bought slaves are the same. So the two groups share the immersion rule, while the adult/minor split from step 11 can still apply only to sons of maidservants.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us
Similar to, the same as
Sons of maidservants, children born in a Jewish household
They were circumcised
They immersed (in a מקוה)

steps.whatToRemember: וכן links slaves and sons of maidservants only on one point: after circumcision AND immersion, neither one makes wine into יין נסך.

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:
slaves are similar to sons of maidservants.

phrases.aramaic: מָה בְּנֵי שְׁפָחוֹת מָלוּ וְלֹא טָבְלוּ
phrases.english: Just as sons of maidservants who were circumcised but did not immerse
are the ones who make wine into libation wine,
but if they were circumcised and immersed, they do not,
so too with slaves.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן, עֲבָדִים דֻּומְיָא דִּבְנֵי שְׁפָחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14 with a new reading of וכן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads the link as being about one point only (immersion), not the adult/minor split.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If וכן is about wine, then slaves and sons of maidservants must share the adult/minor split.
steps.terutzMaskana: וכן teaches only that, like sons of maidservants, slaves who were circumcised and immersed no longer make wine into יין נסך.

steps.title: This rejects שמואל's view that immersed slaves still make wine into יין נסך
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא needed to teach this: to reject רב נחמן in the name of שמואל, who said bought slaves make wine into יין נסך even after circumcision and immersion, until עבודה זרה is gone from their mouths.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is to reject what רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: One who buys slaves from gentiles, even if they were circumcised and immersed, they make wine into יין נסך until עבודה זרה disappears from their mouths. The ברייתא teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows why step 15's lesson is needed. It rejects a view of שמואל that bought slaves stay a problem for wine even after immersion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל thought that slaves bought from gentiles are still used to speaking about idols, so their touch still forbids wine until they stop. The ברייתא, read as in step 15, says no: once circumcised and immersed, they are like sons of maidservants and do not forbid wine.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, to reject (a different view)
One who buys
Until it sinks away, until it disappears
Idol worship

steps.whatToRemember: According to this reading of the ברייתא, slaves who were circumcised and immersed do not make wine into יין נסך, against רב נחמן in the name of שמואל. The adult/minor split stays limited to sons of maidservants, so רב's rule about a gentile baby holds. רב נחמן's view is examined directly starting in step 17.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the ברייתא, read this way, disagrees with רב נחמן: circumcision and immersion would be enough, without waiting for the slaves to stop speaking about idols. This sets up the direct discussion of רב נחמן's view that follows.

phrases.english: This is to exclude the view of Rav Nachman in the name of Shmuel,
for Rav Nachman said in the name of Shmuel:
One who buys slaves from the gentiles,
even though they were circumcised and immersed,
they make wine into libation wine
until idol worship disappears from their mouths.
It teaches us that this is not so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what view the lesson of step 15 comes to reject.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: As the ברייתא is now read, slaves bought from gentiles who were circumcised and immersed do not make wine into יין נסך, against רב נחמן in the name of שמואל. The ברייתא no longer contradicts רב.

steps.title: רב נחמן's rule about newly bought slaves and wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to discuss רב נחמן's statement in the name of שמואל directly. Slaves bought from non-Jews make wine into יין נסך even after מילה and טבילה, until עבודה זרה is gone from their mouths.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now let us look at that statement itself. רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: if someone buys slaves from non-Jews, even after they were circumcised and immersed, they still make wine into יין נסך until עבודה זרה fades from their mouths.
steps.whatsHappening: The word גופא tells us the גמרא is now going back to discuss רב נחמן's statement on its own terms. That statement was only mentioned in passing in step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 16 this statement was only used to explain why the ברייתא needed to teach something. Now the גמרא quotes it in full so it can examine it: how long it lasts, and whether a source contradicts it. The key point is that מילה and טבילה alone do not end the problem, because old habits of עבודה זרה are still on their lips.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': the גמרא returns to examine a statement it quoted earlier
Wine forbidden because it may have been used for idol worship
They were circumcised and immersed, the steps that make a slave part of a Jewish household
That it sinks away, meaning fades or disappears
Idol worship

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion appearing for the first time. It is the same statement of רב נחמן from step 16, quoted again so the גמרא can discuss it directly.

phrases.english: The matter itself:
phrases.notes: This goes back to the statement mentioned at the end of step 16.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Shmuel said:
One who buys slaves from the gentiles,
even though they were circumcised and immersed,
they make wine into forbidden libation wine
until idol worship sinks away from their mouths.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the statement cited in step 16 and opens a direct discussion of it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaves bought from non-Jews make wine into יין נסך even after מילה and טבילה, until עבודה זרה is gone from their mouths.

steps.title: How long does that take
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much time must pass before עבודה זרה is considered gone from their mouths.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how long is that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple clarifying question: how long does it take? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's rule ends at an unclear point: 'until עבודה זרה fades from their mouths.' The גמרא wants a fixed amount of time so the rule can actually be followed.

keyTerms.meaning: And how much? Here it means 'how long?'

phrases.english: And how long?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the time limit left open in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The amount of time until עבודה זרה is considered gone from the slaves' mouths.

steps.title: Twelve months
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי answers that it takes twelve months.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: until twelve months have passed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives the answer: twelve months.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the rule has a clear end point. For the first twelve months after the slave is bought, his touch still makes wine into יין נסך, even after מילה and טבילה. After that, we assume his old habits are gone.

keyTerms.meaning: Twelve months

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב נחמן, as explained by רבי יהושע בן לוי, a newly bought slave makes wine into יין נסך for twelve months, even after מילה and טבילה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Until twelve months.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: עַד שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.

steps.title: רבה challenges רב נחמן from the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבה objects to רב נחמן by quoting the ברייתא about slaves and sons of maidservants who were circumcised but did not immerse. The quote continues past this section.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה challenged רב נחמן: 'If someone buys slaves from non-Jews who were circumcised but did not immerse, and likewise sons of maidservants who were circumcised but did not immerse, their spit and what they step on...'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה starts quoting a ברייתא to challenge רב נחמן's rule. The quote is not finished here; it continues in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same ברייתא first quoted in step 9 and discussed in steps 10 to 15. As step 15 explained, it teaches that once slaves are circumcised and immersed, they no longer make wine into יין נסך. That seems to go directly against רב נחמן in the name of שמואל, who said they still do until עבודה זרה is gone from their mouths (twelve months, according to רבי יהושע בן לוי).

keyTerms.meaning: Sons of the maidservants, here meaning sons born to non-Jewish maidservants in a Jew's home
Their spit
Things they step or press on, such as something they sit or lie on

phrases.english: Rabba raised an objection to Rav Nachman:
One who buys slaves from the gentiles
who were circumcised but did not immerse,
and likewise the sons of the maidservants
phrases.notes: This is the וכן that steps 12 to 15 were discussing.

phrases.english: who were circumcised but did not immerse,
their spit and what they tread upon

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule stated in step 17 and timed in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's rule in the name of שמואל, that bought slaves make wine into יין נסך even after מילה and טבילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא, as explained in step 15, teaches that once slaves are circumcised and immersed, they no longer make wine into יין נסך. That contradicts רב נחמן's rule that they still do until עבודה זרה is gone from their mouths.
